    (hwbudget : 12 * e * ((22 : ℝ) + 2) + 8 * κ + 2 * cost ≤ ε / 2)

statement:
\begin{lemma}[Masked rectangle cancellation]
\label{lem:centered-lattice-cancellation}
Let \(\vartheta\) range over a fixed finite set of finite-order
ray characters with conductor primes in \(\mathcal S\).  Let
\(\mathfrak R_*\) be squarefree with \(q_{\mathfrak R_*}\le Z^{B_*}\)
for a fixed \(B_*\), and let \(W_1,W_2\) be smooth profiles on
fixed annuli.  For \(X>0\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
 \mathcal L_i(X,t):=
 \sum_l\vartheta(l)1_{(l,\mathfrak R_*)=1}
           q_l^{it}W_i(q_l/X).
\]
Then
\begin{align}
 \mathcal L_i(X,t)
 &=c_{\vartheta,\mathfrak R_*}X^{1+it}I_i(t)
   +O\left(Z^{\epsilon_1}(1+|t|)^J\right),
 \label{old-eq:2.18d}\\
 |\mathcal L_i(X,t)|&\ll X.
 \label{old-eq:2.18e}
\end{align}
Here \(J\) is fixed, the constants use finitely many seminorms,
\(c_{\vartheta,\mathfrak R_*}\) is independent of \(X,t\), and
\(I_i(t)\) is a fixed measure constant times
\(\int_0^\infty W_i(y)y^{it}\,dy\).
Both estimates are uniform for \(X>0\), for the stated masks, and
for the finite character set.

Let \(D_{\mathbf b}\) be as in
Equation~\eqref{old-eq:2.18a}, and put
\[
 U_i=X_i/q_{\mathfrak b_i},\qquad
 V_i=Y_i/q_{\mathfrak b_i},\qquad
 T=U_1U_2=V_1V_2.
\]
If \(U_i,V_i\ge Z^r\) for \(i=1,2\) and some \(r\ge0\),
then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 T^{-1/2}\left|
 \sum_{l_1,l_2}
 \vartheta(l_1)\vartheta(l_2)
 1_{(l_1l_2,\mathfrak R_*)=1}
 q_{l_1l_2}^{it}D_{\mathbf b}(l_1,l_2)
 \right|
 \ll Z^{\epsilon_1}(1+|t|)^{2J}T^{1/2}Z^{-r}.
 \end{split}
 \label{old-eq:2.18f}
\end{equation}
Without a nonnegative lower length, the same expression is
\(O(T^{1/2})\).
\end{lemma}
title: lem:centered-lattice-cancellation

statement:
def EulerPrincipalComparisonPerCharacterAt
    {Delta : ℝ} (D : HighDataPerturbed Delta)
    (hfine : ∀j, D.ell j ≤ detectorMesh D.t / 200)
    (F : PerturbedSourceData (momentGeometryOfPerturbed D hfine)) : Prop :=
  letI : NeZero (∏P∈F.S, P) :=
    ⟨fixedPrimeProduct_ne_zero F.S F.exclusions.prime⟩
  ∀eta : Character, ∃C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
    let Y : Fin D.N → ℝ := fun j => Z ^ (D.ell j)
    let T : Fin D.N → Finset PrimeIdeal := fun j =>
      pool (RayQuotient.identityClass F.modulus ⊤) F.S 1 2 (Y j)
    let normer := sourceResidueConstant F.W F.W (∏P∈F.S, P) *
      (Probe.principalScalar Finset.univ Z totalE
        (slotMass T (residueWeights (fun _ => F.w) Y)) : ℂ)
    normer ≠ 0 ∧
    ‖principalPhysicalPool eta F.S T (fun _ y => (F.w y : ℂ)) Y
        F.W F.W (Z ^ sourceLx) (Z ^ sourceLy) Z / normer -
      HeckeSignal.signal (eta.excludePrimes F.S F.exclusions.prime)
        (sourceCorrection eta F.S) (-11 / 16) Z‖ ≤
      C * Z ^ (HeckeZeroSupremum.beta - 11 / 16 - D.sigma)

/-- The same `D.principal_budget` pays the first Euler exponent. -/
title: EulerPrincipalComparisonPerCharacterAt

theorem weighted_dilation_bin {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (S Q P : ι → ℂ)
    (κ U R q L z v xi delta loss epsilon Ccount Cmoment : ℝ)
    (hκ : 7 / 10 ≤ κ)
    (hU : 1 ≤ U) (hc : 1 ≤ Ccount) (hm : 1 ≤ Cmoment)
    (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hqdelta : q ≤ delta / 2) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (hxi : 0 ≤ xi)
    (hcard : (s.card : ℝ) ≤ Ccount * U^R)
    (hselected : ∀ i ∈ s, U^(q*selectedCapacity κ z (v+xi)-loss) ≤ ‖Q i‖)
    (hfull : ∀ i ∈ s, ‖P i‖ ≤ U^(q*L))
    (henergy : (∑ i ∈ s, ‖S i‖^4 * ‖Q i‖^2) ≤ Cmoment * U^(1+epsilon)) :
    U^(-delta*v/4) * (∑ i ∈ s, ‖S i * P i‖) ≤
      Ccount * Cmoment * U^(q*L-q*z/2+(3*R+1+epsilon)/4+loss/2+delta*xi/4-
        11*delta*(v+xi)/84)
title: weighted_dilation_bin

        Z ^ ((ellTau ρ) * (-(4 / 25) + q + mesh) + loss))) =

        realLossTau ρ N v e eps loss mesh + overhead)

private def forbiddenTerminal (env : Environment) (n : Name) : Bool :=
  let forbiddenModules : Array Name := #[
    `OAI.NumberTheory.DirichletL.Hecke.Nonvanishing,
    `OAI.NumberTheory.DirichletL.Detector.FinalAssemblyUnconditional,
    `ZetaZeroFree.Nonvanishing]
  let s := n.toString
  let badName := (s.splitOn "beta_le_seven_eighths").length > 1 ||
    (s.splitOn "ne_zero_of_seven_eighths").length > 1
  let badModule := match env.getModuleIdxFor? n with
    | some m => forbiddenModules.contains env.header.moduleNames[m.toNat]!
    | none => false
  badName || badModule

/-- Every theorem in every requested module is checked, including private
helpers; required roots must be present and must be theorems. The dependency
walk visits types, values, opaque proofs, constructors and recursors. -/
title: forbiddenTerminal

statement:
## Method

The original cubic-theta probe of OpenAI's argument bounds its numerator
pointwise. This proof replaces that bound by a weighted fourth-moment estimate
for the actual smoothed numerator sum. Mellin inversion and the Hecke
functional equation reflect the physical numerator to a plain polynomial of
length at most `U/Y`, and the unused length carries selected prime factors in
the original fourth moment. A coefficient-norm argument controls the original
Euler correction, including its ramified error terms. The moment parameter
stays at the original `κ = 3/4`, with the geometry `ℓ = 167/1000`,
`b = 43/500`, `l_x = 747/2000`, `l_y = 919/2000`, `h = 1587/2000` and
`θ = 11/12 − ℓ/4 = 10499/12000`. The finite exponent comparisons are exact
rational certificates (`evidence/certificate/`). The written argument is
`manuscript/weighted_numerator_proof.tex` (it `\input`s
`weighted_numerator_lemma.tex`); the Lean proof does not depend on it.
title: Method

statement:
theorem mixed_plain_moment (a b B L Mcap ε Cfixed : ℝ)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hM : 0 < Mcap) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ J : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ Z : ℝ in atTop, 1 < Z ∧
      ∀ m q : ℝ, 0 ≤ m → 0 ≤ q → m + q ≤ Mcap →
      ∀ η : Character, (η.modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Cfixed * Z ^ q →
      ∀ R : Ideal O, R ≠ 0 → (R.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B →
      ∀ rows : Finset O, (∀ z ∈ rows, z ≠ 0) →
        (∀ z ∈ rows, (naturalPlainCharacter η z).residue ≠ 1) →
        (∀ z ∈ rows, ((Ideal.span {z}).absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ m) →
      ∀ W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
        Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      ∀ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ, 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ → X₁ ≤ Z ^ L → X₂ ≤ Z ^ L →
        ∑ z ∈ rows,
          ‖polynomial (excluded (naturalPlainCharacter η z) R) false W₁ X₁ 0 t₁ *
            polynomial (excluded (naturalPlainCharacter η z) R) false W₂ X₂ 0 t₂‖ ^ 2 ≤
          C * (compactNorm J W₁ * compactNorm J W₂) ^ 2 *
            (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ J * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ J * Z ^ (m + q + ε)
title: mixed_plain_moment

statement:
# Nielstron: compressed proof and tighter rational bound

This AI-assisted contribution first compresses the ProofCouncil development,
then uses its exact rational certificates to prove all three original target
families at the smaller boundary

```text
874957019420098946128604623 / 1000000000000000000000000000
```

The improvement over `874957019421 / 1000000000000` is exactly
`901053871395377 / 1000000000000000000000000000` (about 9.01 × 10⁻¹³).
This is a modest refinement of the inherited argument, not a claim of the
Riemann hypothesis or a new analytic method.

**Catalogue status: verification pending.** The complete native Lean 4.34.1
build passed on 2026-10-09, checking all 7,232 modules in the selected closure,
including 206 QRH modules. The source build compiled 3,131 modules locally and
reused 4,101 official Mathlib cache modules. Three independently stated literal
rational targets, the original three targets, the strict improvement, and the
public zero-bound equivalences all passed. The only recorded axioms are
`propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

Comparator, NanoDa, and con-ron have **not** checked this candidate. The pinned
checker tools were prepared, but the genuine sandbox preflight failed before
executing proof code. No sandbox checks were bypassed and no signed admission
receipt was produced. See `tightening/checker-evidence/` and the explicit
external-checker field in `compressed/audit/tightening-verification.json`.
title: Nielstron: compressed proof and tighter rational bound

structure MomentGeometry where
  t : ℝ
  N : ℕ
  ell : Fin N → ℝ
  rmin : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  e : ℝ
  cost : ℝ
  eps : ℝ
  sigma : ℝ
  t_pos : 0 < t
  t_small : t ≤ 1 / 100000000
  slots_pos : 0 < N
  slots_injective : Function.Injective ell
  slots_sum : (∑j, ell j) = HighFrontierTargets.totalE
  slots_bounds : ∀j, 0 < ell j ∧ (7 / 8 : ℝ) * rmin ≤ ell j ∧ ell j ≤ (1 / 200 : ℝ) * t
  rmin_pos : 0 < rmin
  epsilon_pos : 0 < ε
  epsilon_small : ε ≤ 1 / 1000
  e_pos : 0 < e
  e_small : e < 1 / 1000
  cost_pos : 0 < cost
  eps_pos : 0 < eps
  eps_small : eps ≤ 1
  sigma_pos : 0 < sigma
  fine_slots : ∀j, ell j ≤ detectorMesh t / 200
  height_choice : ∀J : ℝ, 0 ≤ J → ∃theta : ℝ,
    0 < theta ∧ theta < (1 / 200 : ℝ) / 2 ∧
    4 * theta < (1 / 200 : ℝ) * cost ∧ theta < t ∧
    2 * theta * (1 + J) ≤ t ∧ theta * (2 + 4 * eps) < t

    (hH : RayOrthogonality.globalUnits M≤H) (S : Finset (Ideal O))
    (φ : ℝ→ℝ) (hφ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ) (hφc : HasCompactSupport φ)
    (hφp : tsupport φ⊆Ioi 0) (hφ0 : ∀y,0≤φ y) (hφne : φ≠0)
    (a₀ b₀ B₀ : ℝ) (ha₀ : 0<a₀) (hab₀ : a₀≤b₀) (hB₀ : 0<B₀)
    (hφs : Function.support φ⊆Ioo a₀ b₀) (hφB : ∀y,φ y≤B₀)
    (εm : ℝ) (hεm : 0<εm) :
    ∃c κ K₀ : ℝ,0<c ∧ c≤1 ∧ 0<κ ∧ 0≤K₀ ∧ ∀ᶠU : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀(a ε T allowance Δ ν C height q : ℝ) (i : ℕ),
      1<U → 51/100<a → 2*a-1≤5/6 → 0≤ε → ε≤1/1000 →
      0≤Δ → Δ≤(1-QRH.kappa0)/2 → 0<ν → 0≤C → 0≤height →
      2*Real.pi*allowance+(3*i:ℕ)*T≤height →
      ∀{Label Slot : Type*} [Fintype Label] (B : Batch M H Label Slot U a ε (cutoff (2*a-1) q) T allowance i),
      B.rows.Nonempty →
      (∀u∈B.rows,rowMean B.slots U ((2*a-1)/2) B.binWidth B.widths

        (Fintype.card B.Bin:ℝ)*
        U^(QRH.adaptiveCount (2*a-1) (q/(2*a-1))+

          (Z^(Nstar+shift)) t) v‖ ≤

        Z^((M+507*ε)/2)

theorem fixed_induced_mixed (a b ε B Q : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hQ : 0 < Q) :
    ∃ S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
        Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      ∀ (χ ψ : O → Character) (r : Radial) (R : Ideal O) (Z m X₁ X₂ : ℝ),
        R ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ Z → 0 ≤ m → r.scale = Z ^ m → 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → CenteredExceptionalProfile.InducedBy (χ z) (ψ z)) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → (ψ z).residue ≠ 1) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → ((ψ z).modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Q) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → (((χ z).modulus * R).radical.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B) →
        radialEnergy (fun z => polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false W₁ X₁ 0 0 *
          polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false W₂ X₂ 0 0) r.keep r.profile r.scale ≤
          C * diagonalControl r.profile *
            ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
             (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 * Z ^ (m + ε)

def AllNonprincipalAt (a b radial B L Mcap ε Z : ℝ)
    (J : ℕ) (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : NaturalPlainState Z B radial 1, s.width ≤ Mcap →
    (s.puncture.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B →
    ∀ W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
    ∀ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ, 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ → X₁ ≤ Z ^ L → X₂ ≤ Z ^ L →
    s.energy W₁ W₂ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ ≤
      C * diagonalControl s.radial.profile *
        ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
         (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 *
        (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ J * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ J * Z ^ (s.width + ε)

    (H : Subgroup (O ⧸ M)ˣ) (εm : ℝ) where

  balanced : ∃ K₀ : ℝ, 0 ≤ K₀ ∧ ∀ᶠ U : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀ (a ε T allowance Δ ν C height q : ℝ) (i : ℕ),
      1 < U → 51 / 100 < a → 2 * a - 1 ≤ 5 / 6 →
      0 ≤ ε → ε ≤ 1 / 1000 → 0 ≤ Δ → Δ ≤ 9 / 40 →
      0 < ν → 0 ≤ C → 0 ≤ height →
      2 * Real.pi * allowance + (3 * i : ℕ) * T ≤ height →
      ∀ {Label Slot : Type*} [Fintype Label]
        (B : HeckeDetectorBatch.Batch M H Label Slot U a ε
          (cutoff (2 * a - 1) q) T allowance i),
      B.rows.Nonempty →
      (∀ u ∈ B.rows,
        HeckeDetectorAmplitudeFirst.rowMean B.slots U ((2 * a - 1) / 2)
          B.binWidth B.widths
          (HeckeDetectorPhysicalSelection.physical M H (fun u : FreeRow => u.val)

statement:
\begin{lemma}[Common coefficient under complete extraction]
\label{lem:centered-coefficient-invariant}
For a centered input, the two transforms and the intervening Gauss-row
enlargement just constructed preserve the following coefficient data.
Each Gauss polynomial and each amplifier error retains
Equation~\eqref{eq:centered-coefficient-form}, multiplied by \(G(u,h)\),
apart from bounded frozen scalars and row scalars of modulus at most one.
For an uncentered input, omit the second rectangle throughout.
After the second transform and the full M\"obius factor allocation, each
separated child side has that coefficient form without \(G\) and without
\(s\mid u\).  Every surviving slot has the child's one whole-product
character and its original coefficient \(\nu_i\), with no Gauss coefficient.
Within a side the plain variables have the same character, puncture mask,
and norm power in both rectangles.  The two sides of one squared Gauss norm
may have different norm powers; their inducing characters differ by a
member of \(\Theta\).

If the new inducing character belongs to \(\Theta\), fixing the live slot
labels leaves the plain coefficient
\[
 \vartheta(l_1)\vartheta(l_2)
 1_{(l_1l_2,\mathfrak R_*)=1}q_{l_1l_2}^{it}D_{\mathbf b}(l_1,l_2)
\]
for one \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), one squarefree mask
\(\mathfrak R_*\) of polynomial norm, and one real \(t\).
The mask may depend on the frozen row, but is common to both variables
and both rectangles.  All coefficients are understood with their retained
frozen scalars, including zeros, and the exact normalizations recorded below.
\end{lemma}
title: lem:centered-coefficient-invariant

statement:
theorem fixed_induced_mixed_height (a b ε B Q : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hQ : 0 < Q) :
    ∃ J : ℕ, ∃ S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
        Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      ∀ (χ ψ : O → Character) (r : Radial) (R : Ideal O) (Z m X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ),
        R ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ Z → 0 ≤ m → r.scale = Z ^ m → 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → CenteredExceptionalProfile.InducedBy (χ z) (ψ z)) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → (ψ z).residue ≠ 1) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → ((ψ z).modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Q) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → (((χ z).modulus * R).radical.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B) →
        radialEnergy (fun z => polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false W₁ X₁ 0 t₁ *
          polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false W₂ X₂ 0 t₂) r.keep r.profile r.scale ≤
          C * diagonalControl r.profile *
            ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
             (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 *
            (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ J * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ J * Z ^ (m + ε)
title: fixed_induced_mixed_height

  let V := coordV Q z
  let D := coordD Q eta v x
  let E₀ := unramifiedE₀ Q A eta v x z

  ⟨correctionDefectConstant V D E₀, correctionDefectLinear V D v E₀ E₁,
    correctionDefectQuadratic V D v E₁⟩

def finsetImageEquiv {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (s : Finset α) (f : α→β) (hf : Function.Injective f) : s≃s.image f :=
  Equiv.ofBijective (fun i:s=>⟨f i.val,Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨i.val,i.property,rfl⟩⟩)
    ⟨by intro i j hij;apply Subtype.ext;exact hf (congrArg Subtype.val hij),by
      intro j
      obtain ⟨i,hi,hij⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp j.property
      exact ⟨⟨i,hi⟩,Subtype.ext hij⟩⟩
title: finsetImageEquiv

statement:
def rescale (P : WeakFEPair ℂ)
    (hPf : ContinuousOn P.f (Ioi 0)) (hPg : ContinuousOn P.g (Ioi 0))
    (u : ℝ) (hu : 0 < u) : WeakFEPair ℂ where
  f := fun x => P.f (u * x)
  g := fun x => P.g (u⁻¹ * x)
  k := P.k
  ε := P.ε * (u ^ (-P.k) : ℝ)
  f₀ := P.f₀
  g₀ := P.g₀
  hf_int := (hPf.comp (by fun_prop) (fun x hx => mul_pos hu hx)).locallyIntegrableOn
    measurableSet_Ioi
  hg_int := (hPg.comp (by fun_prop) (fun x hx => mul_pos (inv_pos.mpr hu) hx)).locallyIntegrableOn
    measurableSet_Ioi
  hk := P.hk
  hε := mul_ne_zero P.hε (Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hu _).ne')
  h_feq x hx := by
    have heq : u * (1 / x) = 1 / (u⁻¹ * x) := by field_simp
    rw [heq, P.h_feq _ (mul_pos (inv_pos.mpr hu) hx),
      Real.mul_rpow (inv_pos.mpr hu).le hx.le, Real.inv_rpow hu.le,
      ← Real.rpow_neg hu.le]
    simp only [smul_eq_mul, Complex.ofReal_mul]
    ring
  hf_top := rapid_rescale P.f P.f₀ P.hf_top hu
  hg_top := rapid_rescale P.g P.g₀ P.hg_top (inv_pos.mpr hu)
title: rescale

theorem mixed_plain_moment_radical (a b B L Mcap ε Cν : ℝ)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hM : 0 < Mcap) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ J : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ Z : ℝ in atTop, 1 < Z ∧
      ∀ m q : ℝ, 0 ≤ m → 0 ≤ q → m + q ≤ Mcap →
      ∀ ν : Character, (ν.modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Cν →
        (∀ I : Ideal O, ¬ Supported I → idealCoeff ν I = 0) →
      ∀ (ι : Type u) [Fintype ι] (p : ι → O),
        (∀ i, Supported (Ideal.span {p i})) →
      ∀ e : ι → ℕ, (∀ i, 0 < e i) →
        (∏ i, ((Ideal.span {p i}).absNorm : ℝ)) ≤ Z ^ q →
      ∃ η : Character,
        (∀ I : Ideal O, idealCoeff η I =
          idealCoeff ν I * ∏ i, (idealRowHom (p i) I) ^ e i) ∧
        (∀ k : O, k ≠ 0 → ∀ R : Ideal O, R ≠ 0 → ∀ I : Ideal O,
          idealCoeff (excluded (naturalPlainCharacter η k) R) I =
            if IsCoprime I R then
              (idealCoeff ν I * ∏ i, (idealRowHom (p i) I) ^ e i) * idealRowHom k I
            else 0) ∧
        ∀ R : Ideal O, R ≠ 0 → (R.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B →
        ∀ rows : Finset O, (∀ z ∈ rows, z ≠ 0) →
          (∀ z ∈ rows, (excluded (naturalPlainCharacter η z) R).residue ≠ 1) →
          (∀ z ∈ rows, ((Ideal.span {z}).absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ m) →
        ∀ W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
          Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
        ∀ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ, 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ → X₁ ≤ Z ^ L → X₂ ≤ Z ^ L →
          ∑ z ∈ rows,
            ‖polynomial (excluded (naturalPlainCharacter η z) R) false W₁ X₁ 0 t₁ *
              polynomial (excluded (naturalPlainCharacter η z) R) false W₂ X₂ 0 t₂‖ ^ 2 ≤
            C * (compactNorm J W₁ * compactNorm J W₂) ^ 2 *
              (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ J * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ J * Z ^ (m + q + ε)

statement:
### C.5. Return to the inverse polynomial

Majorize the \(u\)-ball in (C.1) by \(\Phi(q_u/H)\), expand the square, and apply (C.3). Write its squarefree columns as \(gz_i\), let \(e\mid g\) be the mask divisor and \(h\ne0\) the frequency. The zero frequency costs \(O(H\|W\|_\infty^2)\). The inverse-character conversion in (A.1), followed by a fixed ray expansion, gives cubic coefficients. Remove \((z_1,z_2)=1\) by \(z_i=vn_i\). With zeros retained, the change of variables is bijective:
\[
b=g/e,\qquad f=ev,\qquad k=eh;
\qquad e=(f,k),\quad v=f/e,\quad g=be,\quad h=k/e.
\tag{C.19}
\]
Here \(b,f\) are coprime and squarefree. The relations
\(gv=bf\), \(he^5v^4=kf^4\), \(\mu(e)\mu(v)=\mu(f)\), and \(q_g/q_e=q_b\) give one ray component of the nonzero contribution as
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac H{D^2}\sum_{\substack{b,f\ \mathrm{sf}\\(b,f)=1}}\mu(f)q_b
\sum_{k\ne0}\sum_{n_1,n_2}^{*}
&a_\xi(n_1)\overline{a_\xi(n_2)}
\chi_{n_1}(kf^4)\overline{\chi_{n_2}(kf^4)}1_{(n_1n_2,b)=1}\\
&\times W_0(q_{bfn_1}/D)\overline{W_0(q_{bfn_2}/D)}
\widehat\Phi\!\left(\frac{Hq_k}{q_f^2q_{n_1}q_{n_2}}\right),
\end{aligned}
\tag{C.20}
\]
where \(W_0(x)=x^{-1/2}W(x)\). Its support has \(q_bq_f\ll D\), \(q_k\ll D^2/(Hq_b^2)\). On dyads \(q_b\asymp B,q_f\asymp F\), put
\[
X=\frac D{BF},\qquad \mathcal H=\frac{C D^2}{HB^2},\qquad \Sigma=XF=\frac DB,
\]
where the fixed \(C\) covers supports. Since \(H\ge DZ^\kappa\),
\(\mathcal H/\Sigma=CD/(HB)\ll Z^{-\kappa}\). Apply (C.5) with gap \(\kappa/2\), then (1.4) and (C.4). The coupled kernels have uniform derivatives. The dyad is bounded by
\[
Z^\varepsilon\frac{HB}{D^2}\,B(XF)^2\|W\|_{C^J}^2
=HZ^\varepsilon\|W\|_{C^J}^2.
\]
A transformed column scale below one has either empty support or boundedly many columns and is handled by counting; a row scale below one is empty. Sum dyads and the fixed ray characters, and add the principal contribution. This proves (C.1). Complex conjugation, replacing \(\nu\) by \(\bar\nu\), handles the other orientation. For \(W(y)y^{it}\), its finite seminorm grows polynomially in \(1+|t|\), as asserted.

To obtain (3.2), take \(Z=\max(2,D,H)\). For \(D\ge2\) and \(H\ge D^{1+\vartheta}\), the power-gap hypothesis holds with \(\kappa=\vartheta/(1+\vartheta)\). Renaming the arbitrarily small loss gives \(H(HD)^\varepsilon\). Bounded column scales follow by counting. Thus (3.2) includes all element rows and both orientations, with the stated common-profile control. ∎
title: C.5. Return to the inverse polynomial

statement:
### 2.1. One prime-divisibility term and one subtraction

Fix a primitive target \(\eta\). Let \(b_*\) generate the product of the primes in \(S\). Choose a primitive residue character \(\xi\) modulo \(b_*\), quadratic at odd residue characteristic and cubic at the prime of norm four. Thus \(\xi^6=1\) on units. Put
\[
 \tau=q_{b_*}^{-1/2}g_\xi(b_*,1),\qquad
 \Xi(A)=\xi(A)\chi_A(b_*),\qquad |\tau|=1.
\]
Choose nonnegative nonzero annular weights \(W_0,W_1,w\), and set
\[
\begin{gathered}
 V_G(r)=\frac{e^{-(\log r)^2/4}}{2\sqrt\pi},\qquad \widehat V_G(t)=e^{t^2},\\
 \mathcal C_V(N;m,\nu)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf},n}
 \frac{\overline{\alpha(cn^3)}\gamma_2(c)\nu(cn^3)\chi_{cn^3}(m)}
 {\sqrt{q_c}\,q_n}\,V(q_cq_n^3/N).
\end{gathered}
\tag{2.2}
\]
The ideals \(c,n\) may share primes. With \(A=cn^3\), define
\[
 T_{m,a,\eta}(t)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf},n}
 \gamma_2(c)\overline{\alpha(A)G(A)}\eta(A)\Xi(A)^{-1}R(A,a)
 \chi_A(m)q_c^{-1/2-t}q_n^{-1-3t},
\tag{2.3}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
 I_\eta(X,Y,Z)=\frac1Y\sum_a
 &\frac{W_1(q_a/Y)\chi_a(b_*)}{\tau\xi(a)\sqrt{q_{b_*}q_aX}}
 \sum_m\xi(m)q_a^{-1/2}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m)
 W_0\!\left(\frac{q_m}{q_{b_*}q_aX}\right)\\
 &\times\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(4)}Z^te^{t^2}T_{m,a,\eta}(t)\,dt.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.4}
\]
The annular weights leave finitely many \(a,m\), with \(m\ne0\); the remaining sum and integral converge absolutely. Let \(I_{\eta;\mathfrak p}\) insert \(\mathbf1_{\mathfrak p\mid cn^3}\) on the **whole** theta index. At the scales (2.1), the compensated probe is
\[
 I_\eta^{\rm comp}(Z)=\sum_{\mathfrak p\notin S}w(q_{\mathfrak p}/P)
 \left\{\overline{\eta(\mathfrak p)}I_{\eta;\mathfrak p}(X,Y,Zq_{\mathfrak p})
 -q_{\mathfrak p}^{-3/2}I_\eta(X/q_{\mathfrak p},Y/q_{\mathfrak p},Z)\right\}.
\tag{2.5}
\]
The prime weight is independent of the moving row. The conjugate \(\overline\eta\) produces the cancellation in §2.3.
title: 2.1. One prime-divisibility term and one subtraction

## Safe independent reproduction

Use the [maintainer sandboxed replay](../../verifier/liu/README.md):

```sh
/usr/bin/python3 verifier/liu/replay.py \
  --profile /srv/qrh/liu-worker-profile.json \
  --work /srv/qrh/runs/liu-fresh
```

The linked instructions specify the approved baseline, exact binary pins and
operator-owned profile. Every compilation that can load candidate code runs
inside genuine Linux isolation; the canonical challenge is exported first.
The driver's own receipt and logs are written outside candidate-writable paths.
A missing tool, unavailable sandbox or changed dependency is an infrastructure
blocker, never a reason to downgrade the required checks.

The immutable public dossier above describes the contributor's original run.
Its old `reproduce.py`, `build_native.py` and `verify_native.py` are historical
evidence, **not safe reproduction entrypoints**: native compilation inherited

source proof. This package makes no claim to verify every manuscript statement
or the author's broader optimality assertions.

    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 : ℝ) (ha0 : 0<a0) (ha1 : 0<a1)
    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Icc a0 b0) (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Icc a1 b1) :
    ∃C : ℝ,0≤C ∧ ∀(η : Character) (Z : ℝ),1≤Z → ∀R : Finset FreeRow,
      (∀u∈R,u.val≠1 ∧ ((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤Z^(QRH.h+ζ)) →

      (∀P:(∀i,T i),Function.Injective (fun i=>(P i).val)) →
      ∀length : Fin K→ℝ,(∑j,length j)=QRH.ell →
      (∀j P,P∈T j → (P.val.absNorm:ℝ)≤b*Z^(length j)) →
      ∀W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ,(∀j y,‖W j y‖≤A) →

      ‖finitePhysicalRows S hmax η R T W (fun j=>Z^(length j)) W0 W1 (Z^QRH.lx) (Z^QRH.ly) Z-
        finiteCentralCubeRows S hS hmax η R T hT W (fun j=>Z^(length j)) W0 W1
          (Z^QRH.lx) (Z^QRH.ly) Z e a H‖≤C*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^2*Z^(-saving)

statement:
def SameDataNonfloorRows
    {Delta : ℝ} (D : HighDataPerturbed Delta)
    (hfine : ∀j, D.ell j ≤ detectorMesh D.t / 200)
    (F : PerturbedSourceData (momentGeometryOfPerturbed D hfine))
    (wide : WideCountParameters.{0, 0, 0, 0} F.modulus ⊤ D.t)
    (theta : ℝ) (n m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  letI : NeZero (∏P∈F.S, P) := ⟨fixedPrimeProduct_ne_zero F.S F.exclusions.prime⟩
  ∃C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀eta : Character, ∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop, ∀C0 : ℝ, 0 ≤ C0 →
      ∀rows : Finset FreeRow,
      (∀u∈rows, u.val ≠ 1 ∧ Z ^ (1 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ rowNorm u ∧
        (calibrationForSet F.S F.maximal).residueMonoid u.val ≠ 0 ∧
        rowNorm u ≤ Z ^ (PerturbedCentral.physicalHeight + D.t)) →
      ∀idx grid : FreeRow → ℕ,
      (∀u∈rows, idx u ≤ n ∧ grid u ≤ m ∧ grid u ≠ 0 ∧
        51 / 100 + D.e * grid u ≤ 1) →
      (∀u∈rows, detectorMaximum
        (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
          (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
        (3 * (idx u + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) <
          51 / 100 + D.e * grid u + 2 * D.e) →
      (∀u∈rows, 51 / 100 + D.e * grid u ≤ detectorMaximum
        (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
          (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
        ((3 * idx u : ℕ) * Z ^ theta)) →
      (∀k∈ProbeHighRowFamily.smallDyadicIndices
          (Z ^ (PerturbedCentral.physicalHeight + D.t)),
        ∀i∈Finset.range (n + 1), ∀j∈Finset.range (m + 1),
        let rows' := ProbeHighRowFamily.cubeBinRows
          (rows ∩ ProbeHighRowFamily.dyadicRows 1 k) idx grid i j
        rows'.Nonempty → ∀t : HeightSpace,
        ((|t.1.1| ≤ (3 * i + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta ∧
            |t.2| ≤ (3 * i + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) ∧
          |t.1.2| ≤ (3 * i + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) →
        SourceMomentsAt F.modulus ⊤ le_top F.S F.exclusions.prime eta rows'
          D.ell (fun _ y => (F.w y : ℂ)) Z
          (ProbeHighRowFamily.sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k)
          (51 / 100 + D.e * j) D.ε theta (7 / 8) 2 D.t D.t i
          ((17 / 50 : ℂ) + t.1.2 * Complex.I)
          (PerturbedCentral.deltaGap HeckeZeroSupremum.beta)
          (if 2 * (51 / 100 + D.e * j) - 1 ≤ 5 / 6 then wide.cB else wide.cH)
          (if 2 * (51 / 100 + D.e * j) - 1 ≤ 5 / 6 then wide.kB else wide.kH)
          (C0 * Z ^ D.t) (Z ^ (2 * theta)) D.t) →
      let Y : Fin D.N → ℝ := fun j => Z ^ (D.ell j)
      let T : Fin D.N → Finset ProbePhysical.PrimeIdeal := fun j =>
        pool (RayQuotient.identityClass F.modulus ⊤) F.S 1 2 (Y j)
      let normer := sourceResidueConstant F.W F.W (∏P∈F.S, P) *
        (Probe.principalScalar Finset.univ Z PerturbedCentral.totalE
          (slotMass T (residueWeights (fun _ => F.w) Y)) : ℂ)
      normer ≠ 0 ∧
      ‖finiteCentralCubeRows F.S F.exclusions F.maximal eta rows T
        (ProbeHighRowFamily.nonfloorPoolOutside F.modulus ⊤ F.S D.N 1 2 Y)
        (fun _ y => (F.w y : ℂ)) Y F.W F.W
        (Z ^ PerturbedCentral.sourceLx) (Z ^ PerturbedCentral.sourceLy) Z D.e
        (fun u => 51 / 100 + D.e * grid u)
        (fun u => (3 * idx u + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) / normer‖ ≤
      C * C0 * (eta.modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ^ (2 * D.eps) *
        Z ^ (HeckeZeroSupremum.beta - 11 / 16 - D.sigma)

/-- Instantiate the complete central6 nonfloor consumer from the same datum. -/
title: SameDataNonfloorRows

    (Q : ι → ℂ) (M E : ℝ) (hM : 0 < M) (hU : 1 ≤ U) (hxi : 0 ≤ xi) (hrho : 0 ≤ rho)
    (hzero : ∀ i e, ¬valid i e → S i e = 0)
    (hupper : ∀ i e, valid i e → max 1 (L i * N i e) ≤ U^((n : ℝ)*xi))

    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (hfirst : FirstTail (1/4) S)
    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 : ℝ) (ha0 : 0<a0) (ha1 : 0<a1)
    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Icc a0 b0) (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Icc a1 b1) :
    ∃C : ℝ,0<C ∧ ∀(η : Character) (Z : ℝ),1≤Z → ∀R : ℕ→Finset FreeRow,
      (∀n u,u∈R n → u.val≠1 ∧ Z^(QRH.h+ζ)*(2:ℝ)^n≤((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ) ∧
        ((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤2*(Z^(QRH.h+ζ)*(2:ℝ)^n)) →
      ∀(T : Fin K→Finset PrimeIdeal) (hT : ∀i P,P∈T i→P.val∉S),
      (∀P:(∀i,T i),Function.Injective (fun i=>(P i).val)) →
      ∀length : Fin K→ℝ,(∀i,0≤length i) → (∑i,length i)=QRH.ell →
      ∀W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ,(∀i,Function.support (W i)⊆Icc a b) → (∀i y,‖W i y‖≤B) →
      Summable (fun n=>absolutePhysicalDyadIntegral S hS hmax η (R n) T hT W (fun i=>Z^(length i)) W0 W1
        (Z^QRH.lx) (Z^QRH.ly) Z 2 2 r) ∧

        (Z^QRH.lx) (Z^QRH.ly) Z 2 2 r)
      ≤C*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^δ*Z^((1+QRH.lx/2+QRH.ly)+(QRH.h+ζ)*(8/5+δ)-ζ*r)

theorem certified_retained_fixed_profile {D : Cycle25.Weighted.MomentData}
    (F : Cycle25ProbeFinalAssembly.WeightedSourceData D) (κ : ℝ) (hκlo : 7/10 ≤ κ) (hκhi : κ ≤ 3/4)
    (hbeta : (51/100:ℝ) ≤ HeckeZeroSupremum.beta)
    (hκbeta : 2*HeckeZeroSupremum.beta-1 ≤ κ)
    (G:𝓢(ℝ,ℂ)) (loss Cscale Ccond xi:ℝ)
    (hloss:0 < loss) (hCscale:0 < Cscale) (hCcond:0 < Ccond) (hxi:0 < xi) :
    ∃degree:ℕ, ∃C:ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠU:ℝ in atTop,
      1 < U ∧ ∀rows:Finset FreeRow,
      (∀u∈rows, U^(1/100:ℝ) ≤ rowNorm u ∧ rowNorm u ≤ U) →
      ∀(τ ψ:rows→Character) (X:rows→ℝ) (m:ℝ),
      (∀i, ∀n:O, elementCoeff (rowCharacter F.S F.exclusions.prime i.val) n = elementCoeff (τ i) n) →
      (∀i, 0 < X i) → 0 ≤ m → m+xi ≤ 2 →
      (∀i, (Ideal.absNorm (∏P∈sourcePrimes (τ i) (ψ i),P):ℝ) ≤ Ccond*U) →
      (∀i, ((ψ i).modulus.absNorm:ℝ)*(Ideal.absNorm (∏P∈sourcePrimes (τ i) (ψ i),P):ℝ)
        ≤ Cscale*U^m*X i) →
      ∀T:Finset (Fin D.N), ∀width:T→ℝ, ∀z:T→ℂ, ∀height:ℝ,
      (∀i, 0 ≤ width i) →
      (∀i, width i ≤ Cycle25.Energy.commonMesh 2 0 1 (D.t/4)) →
      (∀i, (z i).re = 17/50) → 0 ≤ height → (∀i, |(z i).im| ≤ height) →
      (2*(m+xi)+6*κ*(∑i,width i) ≤ 1 ∨ T=∅) →
      (∑i:rows, ‖retainedSchwartz (τ i) (ψ i) G (X i) (U^(xi/4))‖^4 *
        ‖∏s,HeckePrimeRow.canonicalPrimeAmplitude F.modulus ⊤ i.val.val F.W 2
          (U^(width s)) (z s)‖^2)
        ≤ C*(1+height)^degree*U^(1+D.t+loss)

statement:
### B3.10. Closure and uniform common mesh

Every strict child has nominal width at most \(M-\sigma\) by (B3.63). The actual enclosing width and support corrections cost at most \(C_*\xi\), for one numerical \(C_*\) independent of the eventual slot count. This follows from the single aggregate \(\theta_N\), the two frequency enclosures, the at most two plain clippings on a rectangle, and the fixed list of aggregate lengths in (B3.53)–(B3.80). Every ledger is affine or a positive part of an affine expression in those lengths. In particular the positive-slot boundary changes by at most
\(|\Delta M|+|\Delta A|+5|\Delta z|\), because \(0<6\kappa-1\le5\). Thus \(C_*\) does not grow with the slot count. The one greedy prefix contributes one mesh, not one mesh per removed slot.

Choose \(\rho,\sigma,\delta\) from the bounded real ranges and final \(\epsilon\), with \(\delta\ll\min(\rho,\sigma)\), so that
\[
T_{\rm term}:=\rho+\delta+\rho/6+3\sigma+5\sigma/3<\epsilon/4.
\]
Put \(D=2+\lceil2M_{\max}/\sigma\rceil\), and, still before specifying the fixed slot system, choose
\[
\xi<\min\{\delta/2,\rho\mathfrak m(7/10)/2,\sigma/(4C_*),
                   \epsilon/(16C_*D)\},\qquad
\eta_{\rm mesh}<\min\{\sigma/6,\epsilon/(16C_*D)\},\qquad
\epsilon_0<\epsilon/(16C_*D).
\tag{B3.81}
\]
These choices preserve the comparison margin, padded core and strict width decrease of at least \(\sigma/2\). Every strict child leaves its width band; there are at most \(D-2\) such calls on a branch. Same-band comparisons use only the preceding uncentered stage. Zero-slot reflection is done at most once per plain before centering, and amplifier errors are not amplified again. Thus the induction is acyclic.

Now fix the arithmetic data, profiles and any finite slot count. Form \(H_N\) and the finite support boxes through depth \(D\); choose \(Z\) eventually so large that \(\theta_N\ll\xi\), the whole-dyad tail inclusions hold and the pool avoids all slot windows. In each stage allocate all divisor, ray, logarithmic and prime-density losses within \(\epsilon_0\). For example, mask deletion can assign each of its at most \(N+2\) masses a share \(\epsilon_0/(10(N+2))\); divisor allocations use global bounds \(C_N^{\omega(v)},d_{N+2}(v)^C\ll_{N,C,a}q_v^a\), with one sufficiently small \(a\), rather than a loss per prime. The prime contour displacement costs \(2ez\), so it also fits a share independently of the number of slots. These subsidiary choices affect constants, not the previously fixed mesh.

When at most \(d\) strict calls remain, permit exponent error
\(E_d=T_{\rm term}+(d+1)C_*(\eta_{\rm mesh}+\xi+\epsilon_0)\).
The width-floor, diagonal and exceptional calculations fit \(E_0\); one strict edge uses its child envelope plus at most the displayed stage allowance, by (B3.69)–(B3.72). Same-band comparisons and reflections have bounded coefficient mass included in that allowance. Cauchy averages child errors, and triangle inequalities take the larger one, so the terminal loss occurs once along a branch. Formula (B3.81) gives \(E_{D-2}<\epsilon\). This proves all zero-slot bands and then all positive-slot bands simultaneously for every surviving subset of the original slots.

Finally choose raw kernel-tail orders and all finite profile and height orders backwards by the common-profile lemma; then take one final threshold for their tails, endpoint ratios and logarithmic losses. Each child extra mask is supported on frozen columns or one frozen amplifier prime, so its norm remains polynomial through the finite depth. Exceptional-row masks combine these with the row radical; (B3.77) is uniform over them. Full moving supports remain explicit, including canceled zero powers. This proves (B3.40) with its stated uniformity.

For positive slots the comparison margin is bounded below by \(\mathfrak m(7/10)>0\), and \(6\kappa-1\le7/2\) throughout the proved range. The cost-to-capacity ratio is \((\kappa d)/(6\kappa d)=1/6\). The common mesh therefore works for \(7/10\le\kappa\le3/4\), with the hypotheses and canonical common-profile family in (B3.40). The zero-slot closure is unconditional and restores the fixed nonprincipal rows separately. ∎
title: B3.10. Closure and uniform common mesh

    (F : Finset α) (W : ℝ→ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0<a)
    (hWs : Function.support W⊆Set.Icc a b) (hW : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W)
    (Lmod Lslot loss lo hi κ : ℝ) (hLm : 0≤Lmod) (hLs : 0≤Lslot) (hloss : 0<loss)
     (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) :
    ∃degree : ℕ,∃C : ℝ,0<C ∧ ∀η₀ : Character,∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
    ∀(θ : α→RayQuotient.Characters M H)(w σ v : α→ℝ)(t T : ℝ),
      (∀i∈F,0≤w i) → (∀i∈F,w i≤Lslot) →
      (∀i∈F,lo≤σ i) → (∀i∈F,σ i≤hi) → 0≤T → (∀i∈F,|v i|≤T) →
    ∀(η : Character)(z : O),z≠0 → ∀N : NaturalRow η z,
      (N.character.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)≤Z^Lmod →
    ∀Q : Ideal O,Q≤M → ¬FixedInducingRow η (internalQ Q η₀) fixedBadMask 1 z →
    ∀A : Finset α,A⊆F →
      ‖∏i∈A,naturalSlot N.character (primePool M H b (Z^(w i)))
        (heightCoefficient (fun I=>idealCoeff (relativeCharacter M H hH η₀ (θ i)) I*
          HeckePrimeAnnular.annularWeight W (Z^(w i)) (σ i) (v i) I) t) (Z^(w i))‖^2 ≤
      C*(1+|t|+T)^degree*Z^(loss+κ*(∑i∈F,w i))

statement:
### Section 5: Low estimate

The elementary energy lemma handles the slack variables and both branches of the minimum. Its use of
\[
\frac y4+\frac{(T-y)_+}{2}\ge\frac T4
\]
is valid without an additional sign assumption on \(T\) or \(y\).

For the rescaled tuple, the Gram parameter remains
\[
P_a=Y'^2/Q=q_{b_*}^{-1}Z^b.
\]
The scale conditions needed for the Gram remainder and the row ranges follow from the exact geometry ledger.

The proof applies the general reflected-energy estimate before specializing the geometry. It does not assume that an old optimized low bound remains valid after changing lengths.

The final tuple exponent is correctly calculated:
\[
-d+\frac{(5\ell+d-1)_+}{8}\le-\frac{7d}{8}\le0.
\]
The count of rescaled tuples and their \(q_{p_J}^{-3/2}\) weight are each included once.
title: Section 5: Low estimate

        Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      ∀ (χ ψ : O → Character) (r : Radial) (R : Ideal O) (Z m X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ),
        R ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ Z → 0 ≤ m → r.scale = Z ^ m → 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → CenteredExceptionalProfile.InducedBy (χ z) (ψ z)) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → (ψ z).residue ≠ 1) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → ((ψ z).modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Q) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → (((χ z).modulus * R).radical.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B) →

            ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *

statement:
### B.2. Unmarked energy, including a frozen label

We use the quadratic large sieve [QLS, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2] in the form
\[
\sum_{q_R\le K}^{*}\left|\sum_{q_n\le N}^{*}c_n\chi_R(n)^3\right|^2
\ll_\varepsilon(KN)^\varepsilon(K+N)\sum_n|c_n|^2.
\tag{B.11}
\]
The coefficients are independent of \(R\). The quadratic symbol on primary generators has primitive conductor \(R\lambda^{e(R)}\), where \(e(R)=(q_R-1)/2\pmod2\): adjusting a generator to its primary representative contributes the character modulo \(\lambda\) to this power. A fixed primary square class modulo four fixes \(e(R)\). Coprime indices in that class have primitive product conductor equal to their product, and reciprocity contributes the fixed bicharacter \(R(\cdot,\cdot)\). These are the Hecke-family hypotheses of the sieve. Finite ray partition and transpose duality give the displayed orientation. A fixed row restriction decreases the positive sum; a column restriction is imposed by zero coefficients.

For a squarefree ideal \(f\), set
\[
\Psi_k(a)=\nu(a)\chi_a(k)\chi_a(f)^4,
\]
and, with \(V(y)=y^{1/2}W(y)\), define
\[
T(X;k,f)=\sum_{n\ \mathrm{sf},b}
\frac{\overline{\alpha(n)}\gamma_2(n)\Psi_k(n)
\overline{\alpha(b)}^{3}\Psi_k(b)^3}{\sqrt{q_n}\,q_b}
V(q_nq_b^3/X).
\tag{B.12}
\]

**Proposition B.2 (completed energy).** For every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
\sum_{0<q_k\le H}|T(X;k,f)|^2
\ll(HXq_f)^\varepsilon\|W\|_{C^J}^2
\left(H+\frac{H^2q_f}{X}\right),\qquad H,X\ge1.
\tag{B.13}
\]
The constants and smooth order are uniform in \(f\).

**Proof.** First replace \(f\) by an arbitrary ideal \(g\) and restrict the row to \(u_0s\), with \(s\) squarefree. Write \(s=tk_0\), where \(t\) contains its primes in \(gS\), and put \(H_0=H/q_t\). The residual squarefree row \(k_0\) is prime to \(gS\). Its local exponent is one, so (B.3) becomes the quadratic character \(\chi_{\mathfrak p}(x)^3\). A frozen prime has exponent
\(j_{\mathfrak p}\equiv1_{\mathfrak p\mid t}+4v_{\mathfrak p}(g)\pmod6\), with the fixed-prime part absorbed in the finite sector. This formula includes every collision.

After fixing unit, \(\lambda\)-valuation and a finite ray class, a reflected branch is
\[
S_m[A,Y](k_0)=3^{-m/3}\sum_{n\ \mathrm{sf},b}
\frac{A(n,b)\chi_{k_0}(nb)^3}{\sqrt{q_n}\,q_b}
V^\sharp\!\left(\frac{3^mq_nq_b^3H_0^2}{Yq_{k_0}^2}\right),
\tag{B.14}
\]
times a bounded row scalar. The coefficients \(A\) are independent of \(k_0\). Initially \(|A|\le a=1\), \(Y\asymp H_0^2/X\). To account for \(j=4\), define
\(A_n(n,b)=1_{\mathfrak p\nmid n}A(\mathfrak pn,b)\) and
\(A_b(n,b)=1_{\mathfrak p\nmid n}A(n,\mathfrak pb)\). The disjoint splitting
\(1_{\mathfrak p\mid nb^3}=1_{\mathfrak p\mid n}+1_{\mathfrak p\nmid n,\mathfrak p\mid b}\)
gives, with \(q=q_{\mathfrak p}\),
\[
S_m[AB_{\mathfrak p,4},q^2Y]
=-q^{-1/2}S_m[A,q^2Y]
+\chi_{k_0}(\mathfrak p)^3S_m[A_n,qY]
+q^{-1/2}\chi_{k_0}(\mathfrak p)^3S_m[A_b,Y/q].
\tag{B.15}
\]
The squarefree restriction and all shared-prime cases are preserved. Thus \((a^2,Y)\) changes to \((a^2,q^2Y)\) for \(j\notin\{0,4\}\), to \((a^2/q,q^2Y)\) for active \(j=0\), and to the three pairs
\((a^2/q,q^2Y),(a^2,qY),(a^2/q,Y/q)\) for \(j=4\). An inactive prime does not increase either quantity. In every branch,
\[
a^2\le1,\qquad a^2Y\ll H_0^2q_t^2q_g/X.
\tag{B.16}
\]
Indeed a prime in \(t\) costs at most \(q^2\); a prime occurring to exponent one in \(g\), outside \(t\), has \(j=4\) and costs only \(q\); exponent at least two costs at most \(q^2\le q^{v_{\mathfrak p}(g)}\).

In the following dual sums the star means squarefree, without an \(S\)-exclusion. Split the finitely many squarefree \(S\)-parts of \(n\) before applying (B.11); their symbols are bounded row factors. Keep the actual row cutoff in the joint logarithmic profile of §1.2. On dyads \(q_n\asymp U,q_b\asymp B\), separation gives the fixed-column sums
\[
G_{b,\tau}(k_0)=\sum_{q_n\asymp U}^{*}
\frac{A(n,b)}{\sqrt{q_n}}(q_n/U)^{i\tau}\chi_{k_0}(n)^3.
\]
Their Fourier densities have the common bound
\(\ll(1+3^mUB^3/Y)^{-A}(1+|\tau|)^{-2}\). Cauchy and (B.11) give
\[
\sum_{q_{k_0}\le H_0}^{*}|G_{b,\tau}(k_0)|^2
\ll a^2(H_0U)^\varepsilon(H_0+U).
\]
Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz in \(b\), using \(\sum_{q_b\asymp B}q_b^{-1}\ll1\), now yields
\[
\|S_{m;U,B}\|_2
\ll a\mathcal D^\varepsilon3^{-m/3}(\sqrt{H_0}+\sqrt U)
(1+3^mUB^3/Y)^{-2},
\]
where \(\mathcal D\ge2+H+X+q_g\). The dyadic bounds
\(\sum_{U,B}(1+UB^3/Z)^{-2}\ll\log^2(2+Z)\) and
\(\sum_{U,B}\sqrt U(1+UB^3/Z)^{-2}\ll\sqrt Z\)
give \(\|\text{branch}\|_2^2\ll a^2\mathcal D^\varepsilon(H_0+Y)\), after summing \(m\ge-4\). Equation (B.16) and divisor-bounded branch counts prove
\[
\sum_{q_s\le H}^{*}|T(X;u_0s,g)|^2
\ll(HXq_g)^\varepsilon\|W\|_{C^J}^2
\left(H+H^2q_g/X\right).
\]
Finally write every row uniquely as \(k=u_0sv^2\), with \(s\) squarefree; \((s,v)=1\) is not required. Complete multiplicativity, with zeros, and \(8\equiv2\pmod6\) imply
\(T(X;u_0sv^2,f)=T(X;u_0s,fv^2)\). Apply the last bound at \(H/q_v^2\) and \(g=fv^2\). Its main expression is
\(q_v^{-2}(H+H^2q_f/X)\). Since \(\sum_vq_v^{-2}<\infty\), summing \(v\) and the six units proves (B.13). ∎

Taking \(f=1\) proves (4.4). A log-norm annular partition extends the estimate to \(V_G\): its seminorms are summable against every fixed exponential, so the row-space triangle inequality converges.
title: B.2. Unmarked energy, including a frozen label

statement:
def unramifiedErrorCoefficients (Q : ℝ) (A eta v x z : ℂ) : CubicCoefficients :=
  let V := coordV Q z
  let D := coordD Q eta v x
  let B := star eta * (Q : ℂ) ^ x
  let nu := star v
  let E₀ := unramifiedE₀ Q A eta v x z
  let E₁ := unramifiedE₁ Q A eta v x z
  let c := (1 - V) / (1 - D)
  let a := errorBracketConstant V D B nu E₀
  let b := errorBracketLinear V D B nu E₀ E₁
  let d := errorBracketQuadratic E₁
  ⟨c * a, c * (b - v * a), c * (d - v * b), -c * v * d⟩
title: unramifiedErrorCoefficients

\begin{theorem}[Improved zero-free half-plane]\label{thm:weighted-main}
\[
 \Bstar\le B:=\frac{10499}{12000}=0.874916666\ldots.
\]
Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $\F$, and every Dirichlet
$L$-function including the Riemann zeta function, is therefore zero-free
on the open half-plane $\Re s>B$. Only the pole at $s=1$ of the principal
(trivial) characters is excluded.
\end{theorem}

theorem original_completed_rows_energy (Q : Ideal Eis) (hQ : Q≠0)
    (F : Ideal Eis) (hF : Squarefree F) (m : Eis) (hm : m≠0)
    (hmLam : ConcretePrimeRowBridge.goodLambda∣m) (hm2 : (2:Eis)∣m)
    (hperiod : Q*Ideal.span {(72:Eis)}∣Ideal.span {m})
    (hbad : ∀ P∈fixedBadPrimes,P∣Ideal.span {m}*F)
    (lo hi : ℝ) (hlo : 0<lo)
    (W : ℝ→ℂ) (hWs : Function.support W⊆Set.Icc lo hi) (hW : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W)
    (Ck η : ℝ) (hCk : 0<Ck) (hη : 0<η) (hη1 : η≤1) (rmax : ℕ) :
    ∃ (degree : ℕ) (C Z₀ : ℝ),0<C ∧ 1<Z₀ ∧
    ∀ {σ : Type v} [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ],∀ (Z shift : ℝ), Z₀≤Z → |shift|≤η →
    ∀ (parents : Finset (Ideal Eis)),(∀ I∈parents,I≠0 ∧ (Ideal.absNorm I:ℝ)≤Ck*Z^M) →
      Fintype.card σ≤rmax → ∀ (lists : σ→Finset (Ideal Eis)) (H : σ→ℝ),
      Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (lists i) (lists j)) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,P.IsMaximal) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,ConcretePrimeRowBridge.goodLambda∉P) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,Prime P) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,ringChar (Eis⧸P)≠2) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,IsCoprime (Q*Ideal.span {(72:Eis)}) P) →
      (∀ i,1≤H i) → (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,(Ideal.absNorm P:ℝ)≤H i) → (∏ i,H i)≤Z^z →
    ∀ (Ψ : Eis→*ℂ),(∀ n,‖Ψ n‖≤1) → CanonicalCoefficientClass.FactorsModulo Q Ψ →

            (u.val*ConcretePrimeRowBridge.idealGenerator I)) (CompletedHeight.normTwistedSource W θ)
          (Z^(1+z+shift)) (fun A => ∏ i,if (p i).val∣A then (1:ℂ) else 0)‖^2)≤

statement:
### Poisson representation

The finite transform uses the full modulus \(sb_*A\), including the case \((s,A)\ne1\). The definition of \(F(s,A,H)\) explicitly records that overlap.

The prefactor accounting is consistent:
\[
\frac{X}{q_A}\cdot
\frac{\sqrt{q_s}}{\sqrt{q_{b_*}q_sX}}
=\frac{X^{1/2}}{\sqrt{q_{b_*}}q_A}.
\]

The sixth-power decomposition includes unit factors in \(u\). The zero frequency is removed by primitivity at the excluded primes, rather than discarded without justification.

The positivity proof for \(m_0(1/6)\) is sound: it does not assume that the Fourier transform of the original nonnegative weight is itself nonnegative.
title: Poisson representation

statement:
theorem error_packet_damped_mass (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S)
    (firsteps : ℝ) (hfirst : FirstTail firsteps S) (η : Character) (u : FreeRow)
    (T : Finset HeckeInverseAmplification.PrimeIdeal) (hT : ∀ P ∈ T, Supported P.val)
    (hη : ∀ P ∈ T, IsCoprime P.val η.modulus)
    (x z : ℂ) (alpha eps rho L : ℝ) (hQ : ∀ P ∈ T, (4 : ℝ) ≤ P.val.absNorm)
    (halpha : (51 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ alpha) (halpha1 : alpha ≤ 1)
    (heps : 0 < eps) (heps1 : eps ≤ 1 / 1000)
    (hx : x.re = alpha + 16 * eps) (hz : z.re = 17 / 50)
    (hrho : 0 ≤ rho) (hrho1 : rho ≤ 1)
    (hline : 1 - alpha - 6 * eps ≤ 1 / 2 - rho)
    (hleft : -(1 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2 - rho)
    (hmargin : 1 + firsteps ≤ x.re + (1 / 2 - rho))
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hcap : L * errorProductDeficit u T ≤ 1) :
    Summable (fun e : ErrorPacketIndex S u T => ‖errorPacketCoefficient S hS η u T hT x z e‖ *
      (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ)^(-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) *
      max 1 (L * (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ))^rho) ∧
    (∑' e : ErrorPacketIndex S u T, ‖errorPacketCoefficient S hS η u T hT x z e‖ *
      (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ)^(-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) *
      max 1 (L * (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ))^rho) ≤
      2 * (579 ^ (ramifiedPrimes (markExclusions S T) u).card * Real.exp (1 / 2) *
        errorProductSize u T)
title: error_packet_damped_mass

      (hdis : ∀P:∀i,T i,Function.Injective (fun i=>(P i).val))
      (hη : ∀i P,P∈T i→IsCoprime P.val η.modulus)
      (Pbase : ∀i,T i) (W : ι→ℝ→ℂ) (Yp : ι→ℝ),
      (∀i,1≤Yp i) → (∀i,Function.support (W i)⊆Set.Icc cp dp) →
      (∀i y,‖W i y‖≤Bp) → ∀(x z : ℂ) (alpha eps : ℝ),
      51/100≤alpha → alpha≤1 → 0<eps → eps≤1/1000 →
      x.re=alpha+16*eps → z.re=17/50 →
      ∀(κ : Type) [Fintype κ] (u : κ→FreeRow)
      (W1 : ℝ→ℂ) (a b Y : ℝ), 0<a → Function.support W1⊆Set.Icc a b →
      ContDiff ℝ ∞ W1 → 0<Y →
      ∀(U xi : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (Cu : κ→ℝ) (Ccond : ℝ)
      (Q : ℕ→κ→ℂ) (P : κ→ℂ)
      (R q L zcap delta loss momentEps Ccount Cmoment : ℝ),
      1≤U → 0≤xi → 1≤Ccount → 1≤Cmoment → 0≤q → q≤delta/2 →

      (∀i,((Ideal.span {(u i).val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤U) →

      b*Y≤U^((n:ℝ)*xi) →

      (∀j∈Finset.range (n+1),∀i,U^(q*selectedCapacity zcap ((j:ℝ)*xi+xi)-loss)≤‖Q j i‖) →

lemma mixed_radial_partition (χ : O → Character) (r : Radial) (P : O → Prop)

    (hs₂ : Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b)
    (hX₁ : 0 < X₁) (hX₂ : 0 < X₂) :
    radialEnergy (fun z => polynomial (χ z) false W₁ X₁ 0 t₁ *
        polynomial (χ z) false W₂ X₂ 0 t₂) r.keep r.profile r.scale =

        polynomial (χ z) false W₂ X₂ 0 t₂) (fun z => r.keep z ∧ P z) r.profile r.scale +
      radialEnergy (fun z => polynomial (χ z) false W₁ X₁ 0 t₁ *
        polynomial (χ z) false W₂ X₂ 0 t₂) (fun z => r.keep z ∧ ¬ P z) r.profile r.scale

statement:
\begin{proposition}[Two saturated witnesses]\label{prop:detector-witness}
Let \(u\) have a bin \((i,a)\) with \(a>51/100\), and assume the
loss and height hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:detector-dyads}.
For every \(t\in[1,3/2]\),
and every prescribed \(\epsilon>0\),
after reducing its preliminary losses, there are
\(\psi\in\mathcal X_u\), a zero \(\rho=\sigma+i\gamma\) as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:buffered-bins}, dyadic lengths \(D=U^r\), \(N=U^m\),
and two polynomials \(M_r,S_m\) for the common row character
\(\psi\) such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:detector-note}
 r\le t+O(1/\log U),\qquad
 r+m\ge t-O(1/\log U),\qquad
 |M_rS_m|^2\gg_{\mathcal A,\epsilon}
 U^{\delta(r+m)-\epsilon}.
\end{equation}
Their lengths and individual values also satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:saturated-witness}
 \begin{gathered}
 t-\tfrac12-O(\epsilon)\le r\le t+O(1/\log U),
 \qquad 0\le m\le\tfrac12+O(\epsilon),\\
 |M_r|^2\gg_{\mathcal A,\epsilon}U^{\delta r-\epsilon},
 \qquad
 |S_m|^2\gg_{\mathcal A,\epsilon}U^{\delta m-\epsilon}.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The constants in the \(O(\epsilon)\) terms are absolute on the
stated parameter ranges.  Both polynomials have the same twist
height \(\gamma-\nu\), where \(|\nu|\le cT_1\) for a fixed
\(c>0\) chosen within the cumulative frequency allowance.
Their untwisted profiles form a uniformly smooth annular family.
For each row, both witnesses use one presentation
\(\psi_{u,\vartheta,\varsigma}\), selected by a label
\((\vartheta,\varsigma)\) in the fixed finite set
\(\Theta\times\{-1,1\}\).  The presentation itself varies with \(u\).
The dyadic pair can likewise
be selected separately for each row from \(O((\log U)^2)\) possibilities.
\end{proposition}
title: prop:detector-witness

statement:
### B0.5. Amplitude-sensitive witness and numerator estimates

For the contradiction argument, suppose \(\beta_*>b_0\). For a bin \(q_u\asymp U=Z^d\), let \(\kappa=2\beta_*-1\in[7/10,3/4]\), \(L=\ell/d\). Partition physical main-slot amplitudes into finite classes with exponents \(g_i\in[0,\delta/2]\); error slots and small amplitudes have \(g_i=0\). Put \(q=L^{-1}\sum_i(\ell_i/d)g_i=\delta p\), \(0\le p\le1/2\). Greedy filling in decreasing \(g_i\) supplies, at capacity \(z\le L\), a genuine subcollection with
\[
\prod_{i\in I}|Q_{u,i}|^2\ge U^{2qz-\delta\max_i(\ell_i/d)-o(1)}.
\tag{B0.37}
\]
Discarding one fractional slot accounts for the mesh loss. Adjusting its coefficient by the inverse fixed character, or conjugating the whole witness, matches the physical \(\overline{\psi_u}\) orientation without introducing row-dependent coefficients.

For \(r\le1\), use inverse capacity \((1-r)/2\); for \(m\le1/2\), use plain capacity \((1-2m)/(6\kappa)\). MI, MP and (B0.18) give count lines
\[
A_I(r)=1-q-(\delta-q)r,\qquad
A_P(m)=1-q/(3\kappa)-2(\delta-q/(3\kappa))m.
\tag{B0.38}
\]
**Proof of the row count.** The short-witness crossing is
\(r_*(t)=[2(1-p/(3\kappa))t+p/(3\kappa)-p]/[3-p-2p/(3\kappa)]\),
with \(r_*\ge13/21\), \(1/3\le t-r_*\le1/2\). Thus inverse and plain capacities are at most \(4/21\) and \(1/12\). If \(L>4/21\), the supply suffices. On the inverse branch, decrease capacity to \(z=(1-r)/2-\nu_0\). Then
\[
1-r-2z=2\nu_0,\qquad 3-2r-8z=8\nu_0+(2r-1)\ge8\nu_0+5/21.
\tag{B0.39}
\]
Thus both MI inequalities have positive margins. Smaller capacities use the unmarked estimate with an \(O(\nu_0)\) loss; decreasing the plain capacity is handled in the same way. Set
\[
C_\kappa(p)=\frac{2(1-p)(1-p/(3\kappa))}{3-p-2p/(3\kappa)},\quad V=5/6-\delta.
\]
The short envelope is \(1-\delta+\delta C_\kappa(p)(3/2-t)\); the long inverse envelope from (B0.9) is \(1-\delta+V(t-1)\). Balancing at
\(t=1+\delta C_\kappa(p)/(2(V+\delta C_\kappa(p)))\) gives
\[
R_\kappa(\delta,p)=1-\delta+
\frac{\delta C_\kappa(p)V}{2(V+\delta C_\kappa(p))},\qquad
\#\text{rows}\ll U^{R_\kappa+\epsilon}(1+T)^A.
\tag{B0.40}
\]
The endpoint \(V=0\) uses \(t=3/2\). Without marks, the same balance gives
\(R_0(\delta)=1-10\delta/[3(5-2\delta)]\), \(t=5/(5-2\delta)\).

The physical numerator needs its **own** moment. For one main/error term of (B0.32), define
\[
\mathcal N_u(Y;s,z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(3)}Y^{w-1}\widehat W_1(w)L_{\mathbb K}^S(w,\psi_u)\mathcal H^{\rm term}_{\eta,u,Z}(s,w,z)\,dw.
\]
At \(\Re s=a+16e,\Re z=z_0=.34\), with \(m=\log Y/\log U>1/2\), set
\(z_A=[2\min(m,1)-1]/(6\kappa)\le L\). Then
\[
\sum_{u\text{ in class}}|\mathcal N_u|
\ll Y^{-1/2}Z^{\ell(z_0-1/2)+\ell q}
U^{1/4+3R/4-qz_A/2+\epsilon}(1+T)^A.
\tag{B0.41}
\]
The reciprocal denominator is independent of \(w\) and is estimated **after** inversion.

**Proof of the numerator estimate.** Appendix B4 proves the following coefficient bounds directly from the six-row table. The factors are polynomials in \(Q^{-w}\): \(\deg H_p\le2\), \(\deg\Delta_p\le3\), with degrees one smaller at row primes. Their denominators are independent of \(w\). Off the row, direct expansion of (B0.29) gives
\[
|H_{p,0}-1|+\sum_{j=1}^2|H_{p,j}|Q^{j(a-1)}\ll Q^{-1-\epsilon_e},\quad
\sum_{j=0}^3|\Delta_{p,j}|Q^{j(a-1)}\ll Q^{-a}.
\tag{B0.42}
\]
At a row prime of valuation \(j\), allocate \(\min(k,j-1)\) powers of a monomial shift \(Q^k\) to \(h_r\mid\Lambda_u=q_u/q_{\operatorname{rad}(u)}\); the rest belongs to a free shift \(h_0\). The exact table yields
\[
\sum_k|H_{p,k}|Q^{-k/2}Q^{\delta(k-j+1)_+/2}\le1+CQ^{-c_e},\quad
\sum_k|\Delta_{p,k}|Q^{-(k+1)/2}Q^{\delta(k-j+1)_+/2}\ll1.
\tag{B0.43}
\]
The sharp error at \(j\ge2\) is \(\Delta_{p,1}\asymp Q\): central normalization cancels it exactly, and its shift is absorbed by \(\Lambda_u\). The quadratic error at \(j=2\) contributes \(Q^{1-a}Q^{-3/2}Q^{\delta/2}=Q^{-1}\). No valuation is charged twice.

On the original annular support, \(W_1(q_nh/Y)\ne0\) forces \(h\le C Y\). Retain this cutoff in the coefficient expansion: it gives \(\log_Uh_0\le m+O(1/\log U)\), so all later moment lengths stay in fixed bounded ranges. Inverting a monomial with shift \(h=h_0h_r\) gives \(Y^{-1/2}h^{-1/2}S_{\psi_u}(Y/h)\). Primitive functional-equation reflection preserves central amplitude and gives \(\varepsilon_uS_{\overline\psi_u}(\mathfrak c_uh/Y;W_1^\vee)\), where
\(\mathfrak c_u=3q_{\mathfrak f_u}/(2\pi)^2\asymp_Sq_{\operatorname{rad}(u)}\) and
\(\widehat W_1^\vee(v)=\widehat W_1(1-v)\Gamma(v)/\Gamma(1-v)\).
Thus the dual scale is \(\ll_S(U/Y)h_0\). Before reflection, delete the fixed Euler factors by their finite expansion; restore their natural zeros afterward. The restoring series has mass bounded by a fixed product of \((1-Q^{-1/2})^{-1}\) and only shortens scales. The reflected profiles are common and rapidly decreasing at infinity. Moving their Mellin line just left of zero crosses only the simple \(\Gamma(v)\) pole there, giving \(W_1^\vee(x)=O(1)\) as \(x\downarrow0\). Hence annular decomposition has summable normalized coefficients. The varying conductor changes their scale, not the arithmetic coefficients to which MP is applied. Equations (B0.42)–(B0.43) give the rowwise coefficient mass below. Indeed, after its slot normalizer is removed, an unramified error slot has weighted mass \(P^{-1/2}\sum_{q_p\asymp P}q_p^{-a}\ll P^{1/2-a}\le1\); ramified choices cost a divisor power. The disjoint slots prevent double counting. Hence
\[
\sum_{h_0,h_r}|c_u(h_0,h_r)|h_0^{\delta/2}\ll U^\epsilon.
\tag{B0.44}
\]
Replace remaining plain values by a common-profile scale supremum **before** applying MP. For \(h_0\asymp U^t\), the allowed capacity is
\(z(t)=\max\{0,\min(1,2m-1-2t)/(6\kappa)\}\).
The chosen prime product is at least \(U^{qz(t)-o(1)}\) throughout its amplitude class. Hölder and MP therefore give \(U^{1/4+3R/4-qz(t)/2+\epsilon}\); the fourth root accounts for the gain \(qz(t)/2\). Equation (B0.44) pays \(U^{-\delta t/2}\). Positive capacity uses MP and zero capacity uses MP0. Reserve small capacity decrements for the reflected-scale enlargement and the two finite meshes before taking the limit. Since
\(-\delta t/2-qz(t)/2\le-qz_A/2\), summing these dyads proves (B0.41). Subunit reflected scales are handled by the original Schwartz profiles and assigned nonnegative length zero; capacities are capped at \(1/(6\kappa)\), never computed from a negative length.

\begin{proposition}\label{extended-euler}
The complete correction \eqref{full-correction} has the analyticity
and full-height bounds required by Definition~10.1 of \cite{q30}
in its first Euler region and in the region $\mathcal D_{2,\tau}$
below. One final excluded set $S$ can make the principal slice satisfy
\[
            |H_\eta(s)-1|\le\frac12\qquad(\Rea s>\st).
\]
The central contours can still be moved for the full row sum, with
an external tail whose scale order is fixed independently of the
tail order chosen at the end.
\end{proposition}

statement:
\begin{lemma}[Marked inverse moment]\label{lem:marked}
Fix bounded ranges for the nonnegative parameters \(m,r,z_i\), a bound
for \(|I|\), and positive constants \(c_1,c_2\).  Suppose
\[
 r+2z\le m-c_1,\qquad 2r+8z\le3m-c_2.
\]
Then, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\begin{equation}\label{old-eq:4.1}
 \sum_{\substack{u\in\mathcal O\\0<q_u\ll Z^m}}
       |M_u(Z^r;W)Q_u|^2\ll Z^{m+\epsilon}.
\end{equation}
The implied constant may depend on the fixed arithmetic data, \(c_1,c_2\),
the bounded parameter ranges, and finitely many smooth seminorms of the
tests, but is uniform in the prime supports and their bounded coefficients.
The assertion holds for either common sign \(\varepsilon_\chi\), and for
every subcollection of the slots.  Norm twists of the tests have a fixed
polynomial cost in their heights.  There is no lower bound on the individual
slot lengths other than the existence of their stated prime supports, and
no mesh condition on those lengths.
\end{lemma}
title: lem:marked

def ZeroOnlyAt (a b bΦ B Cfixed L M ε Z : ℝ) (J : ℕ)
    (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : NaturalPlainState Z B bΦ Cfixed, s.width ≤ M →
  ∀ (W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
    Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
  ∀ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ, 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ → X₁ ≤ Z ^ L → X₂ ≤ Z ^ L →
    s.energy W₁ W₂ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ ≤ C * diagonalControl s.radial.profile *
      ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
       (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 *
      (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ J * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ J * Z ^ (s.width + ε)
title: ZeroOnlyAt

statement:
\begin{lemma}[Normalized radial kernels]\label{lem:kernel-seminorms}
If \(\Phi(q_z)\) is a fixed radial Schwartz function, its transform
\(K(q_y)\) for the self-dual measure satisfies, for every \(A,j\),
\[
 \sup_{x>0}(1+x)^A|(x\partial_x)^jK(x)|<\infty.
\]
The bound uses finitely many Schwartz seminorms of \(\Phi\).
For any fixed norm monomial \(m(\mathbf y)\) and compact
logarithmic cutoff \(\chi\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:normalized-kernel-profile}
 p_j\bigl(\chi(\mathbf y)K(Rm(\mathbf y))\bigr)
       \ll_{A,j}\mathfrak S_{A,j}(\Phi)\min(1,R^{-A})
       \qquad(R>0).
\end{equation}
The same assertion with the extra small-argument factor
\(R^{1/4}\) holds for the reflected kernels of
\eqref{eq:uniform-kernel-proof}.
\end{lemma}
title: lem:kernel-seminorms

statement:
#### B2.2.1. The finite theta source

Put \(\check e(z)=\exp(2\pi i(z+\bar z))\) and \(e(z)=\check e(z/\lambda)\). The theta input [DR, (5.4), (5.7), (5.9), (5.12)–(5.17), Appendix A] gives a smooth cubic theta function on \(\mathbb H^3\), automorphic on
\[
\Gamma_2=\langle {\rm SL}_2(\mathbb Z),\Gamma(3)\rangle,\qquad
\theta(gw)=\kappa(g)\theta(w),\qquad
\kappa\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}
=\left(\frac ca\right)_3\quad(g\in\Gamma(3),\ c\ne0).
\tag{B2.5}
\]
The multiplier is one on \({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\) and on the \(c=0\) elements of \(\Gamma(3)\). Let
\[
L(t)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\t&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Theta_j(w)=\theta(L(t_j)w),\qquad
(t_0,t_1,t_2)=(0,\omega^2,\omega).
\]
Translations by \(\mathbb Z+3\mathcal O\) have multiplier one. Thus \(L(\lambda)\) and \(L(-\lambda)\) give \(\Theta_1,\Theta_2\). Also, for \(u_0=s+t\omega\), \(0\le s,t<3\),
\(\theta\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}u_0&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}w\bigr)=\Theta_t(w)\).

For each of these three sources define \(d_H\) by
\[
\overline{\theta(H(z,v))}
=C_H(v)+\sum_{\mu\ne0}d_H(\mu)\,vK_{1/3}(4\pi|\mu|v)\check e(\mu z).
\tag{B2.6}
\]
Their support and coefficient bound are
\[
\mu=u\lambda^h nb^3,\quad h\ge-4,\quad n,b\equiv1\pmod3,\quad n\ {\rm sf},
\qquad |d_H(\mu)|\le27\,3^{h/6}|b|.
\tag{B2.7}
\]
Here \(u\) is an Eisenstein unit. The dual \(n,b\) may share primes and may contain primes of \(S\) other than \(\lambda\). This is the full source support; the primal \(S\)-mask is not imposed on it.

For clarity, the bound follows directly from the cited coefficient formulas. Their ordinary cubic Gauss sums
\[
\widetilde g_3(n)=q_n^{-1/2}\sum_{v\bmod n}\left(\frac vn\right)_3\check e(v/n)
\]
have modulus one for every primary squarefree \(n\), by the finite-field Gauss identity and CRT. This includes the prime \(-2\) of norm \(4\), where only the cubic symbol is used. The possible magnitudes in the three sources are \(3^{h/6+8/3}|b|\), \(3^{h/6+3}|b|\), and \(9|b|\) at \(h=-4\), all bounded by (B2.7). Valuations make the displayed \(n,b\) unique when the representation exists. At infinity the condition \(\lambda^3\mu\equiv1\pmod3\) selects exactly
\[
d_I(\lambda^{-3}nb^3)=3^{5/2}|b|\widetilde g_3(n),\qquad
\widetilde g_3(n)=\chi_n(\lambda)^{-2}\gamma_2(n)\quad((n,S)=1).
\tag{B2.8}
\]
No coprimality between \(n\) and \(b\) is required.
title: B2.2.1. The finite theta source

statement:
### B1.3. Imprimitive Gauss sums and the complete correlation

The two-variable notation
\[
\mathcal G(a,h)=q_a^{-1/2}\sum_{x\bmod a}\chi_a(x)e(hx/a),\qquad \mathcal G(1,h)=1,
\tag{B1.12}
\]
is distinct from the fixed ray function \(G(a)\). At a prime power \(p^j\), with \(j\ge1\), lifting \(x=x_0+py\) first forces \(p^{j-1}\mid h\). The remaining prime sum is nonprincipal if \(6\nmid j\), and is a Ramanujan sum if \(6\mid j\). Consequently
\[
|\mathcal G(p^j,h)|=Q^{(j-1)/2}\mathbf1_{v_p(h)=j-1}\quad(6\nmid j),
\]
\[
\mathcal G(p^j,h)=Q^{j/2}\mathbf1_{p^j\mid h}-Q^{j/2-1}\mathbf1_{p^{j-1}\mid h}\quad(6\mid j).
\tag{B1.13}
\]
In particular the zeros at nonunits survive every imprimitive reduction.

For arbitrary \(u,v\), define
\[
F(u,v;j)=\sum_{\substack{x\bmod u,\ y\bmod v\\vx-uy\equiv j\pmod{uv}}}\chi_u(x)\overline{\chi_v(y)}.
\tag{B1.14}
\]
Expanding the Gauss sums and using additive orthogonality gives
\[
F(u,v;j)=\frac1{\sqrt{q_uq_v}}\sum_{h\bmod uv}\mathcal G(u,h)\overline{\mathcal G(v,h)}e(-jh/(uv)).
\tag{B1.15}
\]
At \(j=0\), a nonzero summand requires \(u\mid v\) and \(v\mid u\), since \(x,y\) must be units. Thus
\[
F(u,v;0)=\mathbf1_{u=v}\phi(u).
\tag{B1.16}
\]

To expose the common support, write \(u=Cn_1,v=Cn_2\), where \(C=(u,v)\) and \((n_1,n_2)=1\). The congruence forces \(C\mid j\). For \(j=Ck\), solve it first modulo \(n_1,n_2\) and use (B1.5). The exact result is
\[
F(Cn_1,Cn_2;Ck)=\chi_{n_1}(k)\overline{\chi_{n_2}(-k)}R(n_1,n_2)L_C(n_1,n_2;k),
\tag{B1.17}
\]
where
\[
L_C(n_1,n_2;k)=\sum_{\substack{x,y\bmod C\\n_2x-n_1y\equiv k\pmod C}}\chi_C(x)\overline{\chi_C(y)}.
\]
Here \(C\) may meet either residual column. The full local table, for \(p^c\Vert C\), is

| Residual columns at \(p\) | \(L_{p^c}(n_1,n_2;k)\) |
|---|---|
| \(p\nmid n_1n_2, p\mid k\) | \(Q^{c-1}\chi_p(n_1/n_2)^c(Q-1)\) |
| \(p\nmid n_1n_2k, 6\nmid c\) | \(-Q^{c-1}\chi_p(n_1/n_2)^c\) |
| \(p\nmid n_1n_2k, 6\mid c\) | \(Q^{c-1}(Q-2)\) |
| \(p\) divides exactly one of \(n_1,n_2\) | \(Q^{c-1}(Q-1)\mathbf1_{6\mid c}\mathbf1_{p\nmid k}\) |

For the first three rows, each solution modulo \(p\) has \(Q^{c-1}\) lifts. If \(p\mid k\), then \(x/y=n_1/n_2\). Otherwise put \(y=(k/n_1)t\), \(x=(k/n_2)(1+t)\); the ratio \((1+t)/t\) runs through \(\mathbf F_Q^\times\setminus\{1\}\). Its character sum is \(-1\) for a nonprincipal power and \(Q-2\) for a principal power. If exactly one residual column is divisible by \(p\), the other variable is a fixed unit and the free unit-character sum gives the last row. This proves the table and \(|L_C|\le q_C\).

For separation, extend this table to all residual pairs by setting the local value to zero whenever \(p\mid(n_1,n_2)\). This produces a periodic coefficient modulo \(\operatorname{rad}C\) in each column. **It equals the original correlation only on the coprime locus.** Accordingly insert
\[
\mathbf1_{(n_1,n_2)=1}=\sum_{d\mid n_1,\ d\mid n_2}\mu(d)
\tag{B1.18}
\]
before separating columns; no common prime can be omitted from this projector.

A second form is useful when a moment induction has already extracted the complete common prime support. If
\[
u=Da,\quad v=Eb,\qquad (a,b)=(ab,DE)=1,
\]
then, without any squarefreeness condition on \(D,E\),
\[
F(Da,Eb;j)=F(D,E;j)R(a,E)R(b,D)R(a,b)\chi_a(j)\overline{\chi_b(-j)}.
\tag{B1.19}
\]
Indeed the congruence fixes the residues modulo \(a,b\). In the remaining congruence set \(x'=bx\pmod D\), \(y'=ay\pmod E\); the unit factors cancel by (B1.5), leaving precisely the displayed signs. One may extend the right side to all \((a,b)\) with \((ab,DE)=1\), retaining all character zeros, but must again use the full projector (B1.18). This is the common-support identity used in both moment inductions.
title: B1.3. Imprimitive Gauss sums and the complete correlation

    (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hdmin : 0 < dmin) (hdmax : 0 ≤ dmax) (hdRange : dmin ≤ dmax) (hrmin : 0 < rmin)
    (hτ : 0<τ) (hε : 0<ε) (hκ : 0<κ) (hcost : 0 ≤ cost) (hmesh : 0 < mesh)
    (hbudget : 8*e*R+κ≤ε) (hgap : ε < rmin*mesh) (hmargin : 0 < margin)
    (hheight : 2*τ < dmin*cost) (hloss : τ*(2+4*eps) < loss)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hfirst : FirstTail (4*e) S)
    (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (ell : Fin N→ℝ) (hell : Function.Injective ell)

statement:
### C.1. Poisson, smooth separation, and punctures

For a primitive character \(\psi\) modulo \(m\), masked Poisson summation is
\[
\sum_{k\in\mathcal O}\psi(k)1_{(k,r)=1}\Phi(q_k/H)
=\frac{H\gamma(\psi)}{\sqrt{q_m}}
\sum_{d\mid\operatorname{rad}r}\frac{\mu(d)\psi(d)}{q_d}
\sum_h\overline{\psi(h)}\widehat\Phi\!\left(\frac{Hq_h}{q_dq_m}\right).
\tag{C.3}
\]
Here \(\Phi\) is radial Schwartz and \(\gamma(\psi)=q_m^{-1/2}\sum_{x\bmod m}\psi(x)e(x/m)\). Insert \(\sum_{d\mid(r,k)}\mu(d)\), write \(k=d\ell\), and use additive Poisson in classes modulo \(m\). Its finite transform is \(\sqrt{q_m}\gamma(\psi)\overline{\psi(h)}\), including nonunit frequencies. The primitive principal character has modulus one and value one at \(h=0\), giving zero frequency
\(H\widehat\Phi(0)\prod_{\mathfrak p\mid r}(1-q_{\mathfrak p}^{-1})\). Shared primes of \(m,r\) are handled by \(\psi(d)=0\).

Smooth quadratic kernels are separated by (1.4).

Möbius inversion and (A.1) remove a puncture without changing \(XF\):
\[
E^{(r)}(H,X,F;\xi,W)
\le\tau(\operatorname{rad}r)
\sum_{d\mid\operatorname{rad}r}E(H,X/q_d,Fq_d;\xi,W).
\tag{C.4}
\]
Indeed write \(n=dm\). The label becomes \(df\), and \(\chi_m(d)^4\) retains \((m,d)=1\). Terms with \((d,f)>1\) vanish. Apply Cauchy–Schwarz in \(d\) and enlarge only the positive injective image \(f\mapsto df\). The normalization \(XF\) is unchanged.
title: C.1. Poisson, smooth separation, and punctures

statement:
theorem family_count_endpoint_from_plain {Label : Type*} [Fintype Label]
    (M : Ideal O) [NeZero M] (H : Subgroup (O ⧸ M)ˣ)
    (hH : RayOrthogonality.globalUnits M ≤ H) (S : Finset (Ideal O))
    (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (hφ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ) (hφc : HasCompactSupport φ)
    (hφp : tsupport φ ⊆ Ioi 0) (hφ0 : ∀ y, 0 ≤ φ y) (hφne : φ ≠ 0)
    (a₀ b₀ B₀ : ℝ) (ha₀ : 0 < a₀) (hab₀ : a₀ ≤ b₀) (hB₀ : 0 < B₀)
    (hφs : Function.support φ ⊆ Ioo a₀ b₀) (hφB : ∀ y, φ y ≤ B₀)
    (εm : ℝ) (hεm : 0 < εm) :
    ∃ A : ℕ, ∀ data : Label → RowData, ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ U : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀ (rows : Finset FreeRow) (χ : FreeRow → Label → Character)
        (a ε T allowance height Cs : ℝ) (i : ℕ),
      1 < U → 1 / 2 ≤ a → 2 * a - 1 ≤ 5 / 6 → 0 ≤ ε → ε ≤ 1 / 1000 →
      0 ≤ Cs → 0 ≤ height → 2 * Real.pi * allowance + (3 * i : ℕ) * T ≤ height →
      ∀ _w : ∀ u, SupportedWitness (χ u) U a ε (t0 (2 * a - 1)) T allowance i,
      (∀ u ∈ rows, ((Ideal.span {u.val}).absNorm : ℝ) ≤ U) →
      ∀ reverse : Label → Bool,
      (∀ u ∈ rows, ∀ label, ∀ I : Ideal O, idealCoeff (χ u label) I =
        if reverse label then starRingEnd ℂ (idealCoeff ((data label).character ⟨u.val, u.property.1⟩) I)
        else idealCoeff ((data label).character ⟨u.val, u.property.1⟩) I) →
      (∀ label m, 0 ≤ m → m ≤ 1 / 2 + 75 * ε → PlainRawAt rows χ label U m height εm Cs) →
      (rows.card : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card Label : ℝ) * (dyadicLength U : ℝ) ^ 2 *
        max (C * (1 + height) ^ A) (192 * (1 + height) * Cs) *
          U ^ (Exponent.R0 (2 * a - 1) + 6 * ε + εm)
title: family_count_endpoint_from_plain

## Appendix B2. Completed reflection and marked row energy

This appendix proves the reflected-energy estimate used in the moment argument. A whole-index prime mark changes the reflection conductor when its local frequency vanishes. The proof therefore keeps the compatible conductor branches until the row and marked-prime phases have separated; a quadratic–cubic large sieve then bounds the remaining norm.

statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{row-energy}
The completed-row factor $B_{m,\sigma}^J$ in (15.1) of \cite{q30},
where $\sigma\in T$ is the finite ray class label, satisfies
\[
 \sum_{0<\N m\ll Q}|B_{m,\sigma}^J(Z)|^2
 \ll Z^{M'+(5\ell-1+d_J)_+/4+\eps},
 \qquad Q\asymp Z^{M'}.
\]
The constant may depend on the fixed windows and arithmetic data, and
is uniform in the moving rescaling prime tuple.
\end{lemma}
title: row-energy

statement:
### 4.1. Signed additive Gram bound

**Lemma 4.1.** For (2.7), with \(P_a=Y^2/Q_0\ge1\),
\[
 \sum_{q_m\ll Q_0}|A_{m,\sigma,v}(Y)|^2
 \ll (1+|v|)^J\frac{Q_0}{Y}
 \left(1+P_a^{1/6}+\frac{P_a^2}{Y}\right)Z^\varepsilon.
\tag{4.1}
\]
The coefficients must have the displayed fixed finite-ray form.

**Proof.** Use the finite correlation \(F(u,v;j)\) of §A.4. It has \(F(u,v;0)=\mathbf1_{u=v}\phi(u)\), and, for \(u=Cn_1,v=Cn_2\), \((n_1,n_2)=1\),
\[
 F(Cn_1,Cn_2;Ck)=\chi_{n_1}(k)\overline{\chi_{n_2}(-k)}R(n_1,n_2)
 L_C(n_1,n_2;k),\qquad |L_C|\le q_C.
\tag{4.2}
\]
The local factors are periodic in the residual columns modulo \(\operatorname{rad}C\), including unequal valuations. Expanding the Gram square and applying row Poisson with a radial Schwartz majorant gives prefactor \(Q_0/Y^3\): the complete transform contributes \(q_uq_vF\), canceling the denominator in the Poisson factor. The kernel at \(j=Ck\) has argument comparable to \(q_Cq_k/P_a\); zero frequency contributes \(O(Q_0/Y)\).

Before separating nonzero terms, extend (4.2) to residual pairs and insert the full Möbius identity for \((n_1,n_2)=1\). Set the extension to zero if a prime of \(C\) divides both columns, and write \(n_i=dm_i\). Nonzero terms have \((d,Ck)=1\). This is an artificial extension canceled by the complete divisor sum, not a correlation formula off the coprime locus.

After ray separation the joint coefficient has period norm \(\ll q_Cq_k\). Its complete mean vanishes unless the sixth-power-free part of \(k\) is supported on \(C\) and the fixed primes: otherwise one column has a nonprincipal local character at a prime independent of its other factors. On dyads \(q_C\asymp C_0,q_d\asymp D_0\) and shells \(q_Cq_k\asymp RP_a\), put \(N=Y/(C_0D_0)\). Four-dimensional lattice Poisson in the two columns bounds the zero-mean sum by
\[
 (1+|v|)^J R^{-B}C_0N^2\min\{1,(RP_a/N)^A\}.
\tag{4.3}
\]
Below the period use counting; above it use integration by parts at nonzero dual frequencies. There are \(O(D_0RP_a)\) choices of \(C,d,k\). The dyadic inequality
\[
 \sum_{i,j\ge0}2^{-i-j}\min\{1,(2^{i+j}/\Lambda)^A\}
 \ll\frac{1+\log(2+\Lambda)}{\Lambda},\qquad \Lambda=Y/(RP_a),\quad A>1,
\]
gives \((Q_0/Y)(P_a^2/Y)Z^\varepsilon\). Exceptional frequencies have \((k)=ea^6\), with divisor-many \(e\) supported on \(C\) and the fixed primes, and \(O((RP_a/C_0)^{1/6})\) roots \(a\). Absolute two-column volume gives summable dyadic weights \(C_0^{-1/6+\varepsilon}D_0^{-1+\varepsilon}\), hence the term \((Q_0/Y)P_a^{1/6}Z^\varepsilon\). ∎
title: 4.1. Signed additive Gram bound

statement:
## Lean statements

`formalization/WeightedQRH/Final.lean` (namespace `WeightedQRH`, with
`open OAI.SevenEighths`):

```lean
theorem beta_le_theta : HeckeZeroSupremum.beta ≤ (10499/12000:ℝ)
theorem hecke_nonzero (χ : HeckeFamily.Character) (s : ℂ)
    (hs : (10499/12000:ℝ) < s.re) (hpole : s ≠ 1 ∨ χ.residue ≠ 1) :
    HeckeFamily.LFunction χ s ≠ 0
theorem dirichlet_nonzero {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) (s : ℂ)
    (hs : (10499/12000:ℝ) < s.re) (hpole : ¬(χ = 1 ∧ s = 1)) :
    χ.LFunction s ≠ 0
theorem zeta_nonzero (s : ℂ) (hs : (10499/12000:ℝ) < s.re) (h1 : s ≠ 1) :
    AnalyticAt ℂ riemannZeta s ∧ riemannZeta s ≠ 0
```

Comparator form, `formalization/WeightedQRH/Statements.lean`, stated exactly
as the challenges in `formalization/ComparatorChallenges/`:

```lean
theorem OAI.riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_10499_12000_lt_re
    {s : ℂ} (hs : (10499 / 12000 : ℝ) < s.re) : riemannZeta s ≠ 0
theorem OAI.DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_10499_12000_lt_re
    {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) {s : ℂ}
    (hs : (10499 / 12000 : ℝ) < s.re) (hpole : ¬ (χ = 1 ∧ s = 1)) :
    _root_.DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s ≠ 0
theorem OAI.SevenEighths.HeckeFamily.LFunction_ne_zero_of_10499_12000_lt_re
    (χ : Character) {s : ℂ} (hs : (10499 / 12000 : ℝ) < s.re)
    (hpole : ¬ (χ.residue = 1 ∧ s = 1)) : LFunction χ s ≠ 0
```

Tracker-template form: `evidence/kernels/src/Challenge.lean` is the tracker's
fixed three-target template `public/proofs/palomar-20261009/qrh/src/Challenge.lean`
(SHA-256 `eee59775c5f4f892199f7456f85f7664a14ef3010fc1b3df97ed2c0f8a1db4e6`)
with only the literal `874957019421 / 1000000000000` replaced by `10499 / 12000`
in all three statements (SHA-256
`4624fc67bbd5792408525558a48481a5cd3acd258c78caf1ec4d29528703c287`). The module
`Solution` (`evidence/kernels/src/Solution.lean`) imports
`WeightedQRH.Statements` and proves `QRHPalomar.allDirichlet`,
`QRHPalomar.zeta` and `QRHPalomar.allHecke` from the endpoints. The catalogue
entrypoint, like those of the earlier records, names the development's own
theorem: module `WeightedQRH.Statements`, declaration
`OAI.DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_10499_12000_lt_re`, which
`lake build` in `formalization/` builds and which `QRHPalomar.allDirichlet`
restates. `Solution` itself is not a module of the Lake workspace.

`formalization/WeightedQRH/FinalAxioms.lean` prints the axioms of ten
declarations, including the seven above; each depends only on `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. `WeightedQRH.theta_lt_public`
(`Parameters.lean`) proves `theta < 874957019420098946128604623 / 10^27`, the
bound listed by the tracker at main `40844a7`; the exact difference is
`121058260296838385813869/3000000000000000000000000000` (about 4.0353 × 10⁻⁵).
title: Lean statements

    (hH : DifferentiableOn ℂ H {s : ℂ | theta < s.re})

    {a C : ℝ} (ha : theta < a) (ha2 : a ≤ 2) (hβ : HeckeZeroSupremum.beta < a)
    (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hR : ∀ s : ℂ, a ≤ s.re → ‖HeckeReciprocal.reciprocal χ s‖ ≤ C*(1+|s.im|^2))
    (S : Finset κ) (T : κ → Finset ι) (w Q : κ → ι → ℝ) (A η : κ → ι → ℂ)
    {P Z : ℝ} (h : SlotBounds S T w Q A η P) (hZ : 1 ≤ Z) :

      ‖slotResidue χ H a Z S T w Q A η - HeckeSignal.signal χ H signalShift Z‖ ≤
        (HeckeSignalShift.infinityConstant a C 2 * slotErrorConstant S) *
          Z^(a+signalShift) * P^(-theta)
